newsitem.title: USA: U.S. group files suit against NAFTA trade treaty.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group files suit against NAFTA trade treaty.

text.p: A U.S. coalition Thursday said it had filed a lawsuit against the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), charging that it violates the Constitution of the United States and its Bill of Rights.

The American Coalition for Competitive Trade, which said it represents 21 organizations representing over 500,000 members, said it had lodged its complaint with the U.S. Court of Appeals in the District of Columbia.

The group argued that Chapter 19 of the 1994 treaty, which establishes a system of binational arbitration panels to settle trade disputes, clashes with several articles of the U,S, Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

"We hope the Court of Appeals will hand down a favorable decision in this case and, if it is challenged, we further hope the Supreme Court will hear the case before the year is out and before any further devastation is done to our country," coalition president William Gill said.

The coalition's suit contended that, in joining NAFTA, Congress and President Clinton exceeded their constitutional authority by delegating the judicial powers of the United States to the binational arbitration panels.
The coalition further alleged that the pact deprived its members of their right to due process under the laws as guaranteed by the Fifth Amendment of the Bill of Rights.
To buttress his argument, Gill said that 44 of the first 47 disputes handled by NAFTA arbitration panels went against the United States.
Other members of the group criticized the NAFTA, saying that it caused a surge in drug trafficking from Mexico and weakened the U.S. "defense industrial base."
A lawyer for the group said that a similar challenge had been made in the past, but added that it was dropped after the involved parties reached a private settlement.
